To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a method of detecting carried objects from video of pedestrians is presented; (ii) the method is based on a comparison between a pedestrian’s silhouette and a view-specific representation of the silhouette of a pedestrian carrying a backpack or a suitcase; (iii) the method outperforms previous state-of-the-art on a standard test set; and (iv) the method could be adapted to other problems where the object of interest has a periodic appearance
a method for detecting carried objects in sequences of pedestrians has been developed, tested and shown to outperform the state of the art.

a) the use of exemplars for carried objects is more effective than periodicity analysis for distinguishing carried objects from other objects, and b) the use of spatial context is more effective than temporal context for distinguishing carried objects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods for detecting objects from video sequences.
the detection of carried objects from sequences of walking pedestrians.
the detection of carried objects in sequences of walking pedestrians.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to detect carried objects in video sequences of pedestrians with high accuracy.
the method presented is the state-of-the-art for detecting carried objects from video sequences.
the new method has a higher accuracy than the old method and the new method is more robust to noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the new method has improved the state-of-the-art for detecting objects carried on pedestrians, and the new method is more robust to segmentation errors, more accurate in its detection, and has a lower false alarm rate.
the proposed method can detect carried objects in a more robust way.
we propose a novel method for detecting objects that are carried by a pedestrian.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a good prior model for carried objects is essential for good detection performance.

the detection of objects from sequences of walking pedestrians can be improved substantially by using a combination of a temporal-template representation of shape and motion, a likelihood map of protrusion and a spatially continuous model.
the use of prior probabilities can be a powerful tool for object detection.
